metadata.title: AI compute could be a ‘growth wildcard’ for SpaceX - MarketWatch

content.text:
13 hours ago
AI compute could be a ‘growth wildcard’ for SpaceX
SpaceX's acquisition of xAI in February has added a large AI infrastructure business to the space launch company, with Colossus I and II being key assets, Global X director of thematic research Tejas Dessai wrote in a Thursday note.
The acquisition has created synergies and "long-term optionality" for SpaceX, Dessai said, pointing to the company's recent deals with Anthropic and Google. "AI compute is the growth wildcard in the SpaceX story," he added.
In January, SpaceX formally submitted an application to the Federal Communications Commission's Space Bureau for an orbital data-center constellation of up to 1 million satellites. While orbital data centers seem highly speculative today, research from Google suggests that launch prices could fall to an an economically feasible level of $200/kilogram by the mid-2030s, down from roughly $1,500/kilogram today.
